newsitem.title: USA: MGM Grand to spend $700 million on Vegas expansion.
newsitem.headline: MGM Grand to spend $700 million on Vegas expansion.

text.p: MGM Grand Inc., owner of the massive $1.1 billion MGM Grand resort/casino, on Tuesday unveiled a $700 million expansion that boosts its number of upscale rooms and appeals to high-rolling gamblers.

The company is already over a year-and-a-half into a $250 million expansion that has refocused its theme away from the "Emerald City" of the movie "Wizard of Oz" to a "City of Entertainment" with lots of glitz and gloss from Hollywood.

Now it will add a new 1,500-room Marriott Marquis and 500-room Ritz Carlton hotel to the property, increase the size of its casinos, spa and conference facilities and build a "Mansion" with 30 private suites that will cater to deep-pocketed gamblers from around the world.

"In order to stay at the 'Mansion' you have to have a major credit line," MGM Grand President Alex Yemenidjian said in Las Vegas at the Oppenheimer Gaming and Lodging investor conference where the expansion was announced.
"It doesn't matter whether you are Bill Clinton or Bill Gates, you have to have a major credit line," he added with a smile.

The key piece of the project is the Marriott Marquis, which will be located off the strip, behind the MGM Grand's current 5,000-room hotel. MGM will build the hotel and its casino, and Marriott will operate it under a management contract. Marriott Marquis hotels are franchised by Marriott International Inc.
Marriott's global reservation system will funnel tourists to the MGM Grand, helping boost its occupancy before the Marriott Marquis opens and after its opening, which is scheduled for fall 1999.

Yemenidjian said Marriott currently receives about 10 million calls a year for reservations in Las Vegas, but it does not have a hotel here to book. In a rough calculation, he figured Marriott's reservation system could add $24.6 million to MGM's profit on a pretax basis over the next two years.
"If business does slow down in Las Vegas, having that reservation system behind us is the second-best insurance we can have," Yemenidjian said.
The first, he said, is having a beautiful and inviting resort. He also stressed he does not believe business is slowing or that it will be hurt by the city's current building boom.

To accomodate the Marriott Marquis and its grounds, MGM will reduce the size of its long-struggling theme park from 33 acres to 18 acres. The park has been a money loser since it opened in 1993, but it has generated traffic into the hotel and casino. Because of its role as a significant entertainment venue in a "City of Entertainment," the park's popular rides like the new "Sky Screamer" will remain, while unpopular attractions will be rooted out.

The Ritz Carlton hotel will be on an exclusive plot of land adjacent to the MGM Grand/Marriott campus. Groundbreaking for the Ritz will likely not take place until after 2000, and a completion date has yet to be set.

The expansion also includes an additional 30,000 square feet of casino space, a new entry point from the Strip with a 42-foot bronze sculpture of MGM Grand's lion mascot, and the $30 million "Shangri-La" pool and spa.
MGM Grand shares fell 25 cents to $37.75, while Marriott International rose 75 cents to $58.125 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
